entities.summary:
Cassone della Torre, also known as Mosca, was a pivotal figure in medieval Italian history, serving as Archbishop of Milan from 1308 to 1316 and Patriarch of Aquileia from 1317 to 1318.

As a member of the Torriani family, Cassone della Torre played a crucial role in shaping the political landscape of Northern Italy during the late 13th century.

His tenure as Archbishop of Milan was marked by significant events, including the ongoing struggle against the Holy Roman Empire and the rise of the city-state of Venice.

Cassone della Torre's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, influencing the course of Italian politics and church governance for centuries to come.

Like many of his contemporaries, Cassone della Torre left behind a lasting cultural footprint, his name becoming synonymous with the complex web of power and influence that defined the medieval Mediterranean.

As historian Edward Hutton once noted, 'The reign of Cassone della Torre represents the zenith of the Torriani power, and marks the beginning of a new era in the relations between the church and the city-state of Milan.'
